note: Attacker-controlled bytes are read directly from the network into the stack buffer and the length is preserved for later dispatch.
The first byte selects the vulnerable path; sending 'B' routes the same attacker-controlled buffer and length into the stack-overflow handler.
The sink function allocates only an 8-byte stack buffer, establishing the fixed-size destination that will be overrun.
The full attacker-controlled length is copied into the tiny stack buffer without bounds checking, causing stack memory corruption and crash potential.
